honest_c3: C3-1 (commissioned 3 fixes vs total path): The 3 fixes BG-theta-prime was commissioned to apply (safetensors-clone, param-view-split, tokenizer-reorder) all PASS. However, the OPT-1 prereq is end-to-end load-and-forward, and there are now 2 NEWLY-EXPOSED upstream blockers (legacy decoder_v3 forward bug + HF import chain) that were previously masked by the safetensors-save abort. Strict scope reading = PARTIAL. Practical reading = v2 advanced the prereq from 'cannot save' to 'saves cleanly, cannot run forward', which is real progress (~50% of the original gate). Verdict reflects strict reading.

C3-2 (param-delta false alarm): The v1 verdict's loud '-53.3M' delta caused real concern. v2 root-cause: best.pt has all 530.99M params intact (3 separate embeddings 49.15M each, blocks 383.54M, ln_f 0.768K, tension_proj 0.768K, total 530,994,816 verified). The 'delta' was a measurement-view confusion (.parameters() post-tie vs state_dict raw). v2 emits both views explicitly so future runs cannot re-trigger this false alarm.

C3-3 (Fix A: clone vs save_pretrained): Pre-clone (A2) costs ~187 MB extra disk vs save_pretrained-with-tied-keys (A1). For a one-shot conversion checkpoint that lm-eval will load once and discard, A2 is acceptable. If/when this checkpoint is uploaded to HF Hub for downstream consumers, A1 retrofit would save ~187 MB per download. Flag for future v3 if hub-publish becomes a goal.

C3-4 (out-of-scope blockers exposed not introduced): Both NEW blockers (decoder_v3 forward-unpack + HF transitive-import) existed in the upstream code BEFORE BG-theta-prime; they were latent because v1 aborted at safetensors-save. v2 advancing past save UNCOVERED them, did not CREATE them. The shim itself is clean for the 3 commissioned fixes.

C3-5 (verify-path coupling brittle): Shim's --verify path runs `model(ref_input)` directly on the in-memory ConsciousDecoderV3 BEFORE any HF wrapper is involved. The decoder_v3 forward bug surfaces here. Even fixing the HF import chain wouldn't make --verify pass — that requires fixing decoder_v3.py:169 itself. v3 should consider either making --verify load-only (no forward) or fixing legacy decoder_v3 unpack. The latter is upstream-policy-touching.

C3-6 (wall time): 27.5s actual vs 30-60min shim estimate — shim's estimate was stale (assumed slow disk + GPU); CPU + fast NVMe completed quickly. Both v2 fixes worked at speed. Re-running v3 (after the 2 remaining blockers are addressed) will be similar wall.
